_status: Module 4 learner guide, Audit rules (21 October 2026): the five rules, and why scope is a legal line (RA 10175 Sec. 4(a)(1)). Cases invented to practise the rules before signing.

items.text: To check a finding, you open your own office's portal and try a few passwords.

facts.v: Do not scan, probe or sign in to any real system, including your own office's

items.reason: Accessing a computer system without right is illegal access under RA 10175, Section 4(a)(1). Scope is a legal line, not a courtesy.

items.text: You ask the facilitator what "MFA: App" means in Exhibit B.

facts.v: You may ask the facilitator about the rules or the records, not for answers

items.reason: Questions about the records are fine. "Is this a finding?" is not.

items.text: To make a finding feel real, you write the name of a colleague from your own office.

facts.v: Never add real names, accounts or data to your findings

items.reason: Everything in the Audit File is fictional, and your findings stay that way.

items.text: You talk an idea through with the person beside you, then write the finding in your own words.

facts.v: Individual. You may talk ideas through with the person beside you, but every word you submit is your own

items.reason: Talking is allowed; copying is not.

items.text: You search the internet for the vendor named in Exhibit E to learn more about it.

facts.v: Work only from the Module 4 audit file. Everything in it is fictional

items.reason: The vendor does not exist. Your evidence is the exhibit and row, nothing else.
